habitats.name: Arctic
habitats.description: Very cold, icy and snowy. Long dark winters.

animals.name: Polar Bear
animals.environment: Freezing ice and cold sea water in the far north.

adaptations.why: A layer of fat up to 10 cm thick keeps the bear warm in icy water.
Helps it hide in the snow so it can sneak up on seals.
Dark skin soaks up heat from the sun.
Spread its weight so it does not fall through thin ice, and work like paddles for swimming.

animals.wonder: Why do you think polar bears have small ears?

animals.name: Arctic Fox
animals.environment: Snowy tundra that turns brown and rocky in summer.

adaptations.why: White in winter and brown in summer, so it is always camouflaged.
Fur on the bottom of its paws keeps its feet warm on the ice.
It wraps its tail around its body like a blanket when it sleeps.
It can hear small animals moving under the snow.

animals.wonder: What might happen to an arctic fox if the snow came late one year?

animals.name: Walrus
animals.environment: Cold Arctic seas and floating ice.

adaptations.why: Used like hooks to pull its heavy body out of the water onto the ice.
Help it feel for clams in the dark mud on the sea floor.
Keeps it warm in freezing water.

animals.wonder: How are the walrus and the polar bear the same?

animals.name: Snowy Owl
animals.environment: Open, treeless Arctic tundra.

adaptations.why: Thick feathers cover its feet like warm slippers.
Help it hide against the snow.
Lets it find lemmings moving under the snow.
It can hunt during the long summer days when the sun never sets.

animals.wonder: Most owls hunt at night. Why might a snowy owl hunt in the day?

animals.name: Narwhal
animals.environment: Icy Arctic waters, often under sea ice.

adaptations.why: A long tooth that can sense changes in the water around it.
Keeps it warm in freezing water.
Lets it swim close under the ice without getting hurt.
Can dive very deep to find fish and squid.

animals.wonder: Why would a fin on its back be a problem for a narwhal?

habitats.name: Desert
habitats.description: Hot and dry with very little water. Nights can be cold.

animals.name: Camel
animals.environment: Hot, dry, sandy deserts with very little water or food.

adaptations.why: Stores energy so the camel can go a long time without food.
Two rows of eyelashes keep sand out of its eyes.
It can shut its nose during sandstorms.
Stop it from sinking into soft sand.

animals.wonder: Does a camel's hump hold water? How could you find out?

animals.name: Fennec Fox
animals.environment: The Sahara Desert, very hot in the day and cold at night.

adaptations.why: Let heat escape from its body to keep it cool, and help it hear insects underground.
Camouflage in the sand.
It is active at night when it is cooler, and sleeps in a burrow during the hot day.
Protect its feet from the burning hot sand.

animals.wonder: Compare the fennec fox's ears with the arctic fox's ears. Why are they different?

animals.name: Thorny Devil
animals.environment: Dry, sandy deserts of Australia.

adaptations.why: Sharp spikes make it hard for predators to eat.
Tiny grooves in its skin carry dew and water straight to its mouth.
A bump on its neck tricks predators into biting the wrong place.

animals.wonder: How else could an animal get water in a desert?

animals.name: Scorpion
animals.environment: Hot, dry deserts all over the world.

adaptations.why: A waxy covering stops its body from losing water.
Used to catch food and protect itself.
Hides under rocks in the day and comes out in the cool night.
Can survive for months without eating.

animals.wonder: Why is hiding under a rock a good idea in the desert?

animals.name: Roadrunner
animals.environment: Dry deserts of North America.

adaptations.why: Can run very fast to catch lizards and escape predators.
Gets most of the water it needs from the animals it eats.
Spreads its feathers in the morning sun to warm up after a cold night.

animals.wonder: Why would a desert bird need to warm up in the morning?

habitats.name: Rainforest
habitats.description: Hot, wet and full of tall trees and plants.

animals.name: Sloth
animals.environment: High up in the trees of the rainforest.

adaptations.why: Hook onto branches so it can hang upside down, even when asleep.
Saves energy because its leafy food has little energy in it.
Tiny plants grow in its fur and help it blend in with the trees.

animals.wonder: Why might being slow actually help a sloth stay safe?

animals.name: Toucan
animals.environment: The treetops of rainforests in South America.

adaptations.why: Reaches fruit on thin branches that cannot hold its weight.
Helps it cool down in the hot rainforest.
Help toucans find each other among the colourful leaves and flowers.

animals.wonder: What other animals have beaks shaped for the food they eat?

animals.name: Poison Dart Frog
animals.environment: The damp rainforest floor in Central and South America.

adaptations.why: Warn predators: 'Don't eat me, I am poisonous!'
Keeps it safe from animals that want to eat it.
Help it climb on wet leaves.

animals.wonder: Why do some animals hide, but this frog wants to be seen?

animals.name: Jaguar
animals.environment: Thick rainforests of Central and South America.

adaptations.why: Spots blend in with the light and shadows on the forest floor.
Have a very powerful bite to catch its prey.
Can hunt fish and turtles in rivers.

animals.wonder: How do a jaguar's spots help it hunt?

animals.name: Orangutan
animals.environment: High in the rainforest trees of Borneo and Sumatra.

adaptations.why: Help it swing and reach between branches.
Grip branches tightly, so it can hold on with all four limbs.
Builds a new bed of leaves high in the trees every night.

animals.wonder: Why might an orangutan sleep in the trees instead of on the ground?

habitats.name: Ocean
habitats.description: Salty water. Deep, dark and cold in some places.

animals.name: Shark
animals.environment: Oceans all around the world.

adaptations.why: Its smooth shape helps it swim fast through the water.
Take oxygen out of the water so it can breathe.
When a tooth falls out, a new one moves forward to replace it.
Helps it find food from far away.

animals.wonder: Why are many fast swimmers shaped like a shark?

animals.name: Octopus
animals.environment: Rocky sea floors and coral reefs.

adaptations.why: Can change colour in less than a second to hide.
Squirts a dark cloud to confuse predators while it escapes.
Can squeeze into tiny cracks to hide.
Grip rocks and catch food.

animals.wonder: Which adaptation would you most like to have? Why?

animals.name: Sea Turtle
animals.environment: Warm oceans; they come onto beaches to lay eggs.

adaptations.why: Strong flippers work like paddles for swimming long distances.
Protects its body from predators.
Can stay underwater for a long time while resting.
Special 'tears' remove extra salt from its body.

animals.wonder: How are a sea turtle's flippers different from a tortoise's legs?

animals.name: Jellyfish
animals.environment: Oceans all over the world, from the surface to the deep sea.

adaptations.why: Tiny stingers catch small animals for food.
Makes it hard for predators to see.
Drifts with the ocean currents to save energy.

animals.wonder: A jellyfish has no brain. How do you think it survives?

animals.name: Dolphin
animals.environment: Warm and cool oceans all around the world.

adaptations.why: Breathes air through a hole on top of its head.
Makes clicks and listens for echoes to find food.
Its smooth shape helps it swim fast.
Pods work together to hunt and stay safe.

animals.wonder: How are a dolphin and a shark the same? How are they different?
